key_insight: DiffVortex compresses the Biot–Savart kernel rather than the flow state, combining tensor-network acceleration with flexible Lagrangian vortex simulation.
engineering_relevance: Its differentiable GPU implementation supports incompressible-flow simulation around moving and deforming bodies, with gradients propagated through time integration.
method: Evolve vorticity as Lagrangian particles and represent bodies with bound vortex sheets.
Use QTT compression and tensor cross interpolation to precompute fast-multipole moment-to-local contractions.
Prove that kernel QTT rank r yields convolution MPO rank at most 2^d r, independent of grid resolution.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports up to 6.7×10^7 particles on one GPU, validation against cylinder-flow references and elliptical-vortex solutions, and demonstrations with rigid, multiple, and deforming bodies.
watch_item: Compression efficiency depends on manageable tensor ranks; the reported flow demonstrations are two-dimensional.
paper_title: DiffVortex: A quantum-inspired fast solver for incompressible flows
